title.justification: The title directly reflects the core subject of this paper, discussing the equilibria in reinforcement learning training processes.
title.quote: T RAINING E QUILIBRIA IN R EINFORCEMENT L EARN ING

extractions.description: This paper investigates the presence of multiple equilibria in reinforcement learning algorithms within partially observable environments. It highlights how these equilibria can be suboptimal despite full exploration and flexible policy parametrization. The study reveals that memory-oriented policies can lead to more optimal equilibria and explores the role of parameter noise in enhancing convergence.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on the technical and theoretical aspects of reinforcement learning in partially observable environments, without addressing direct implications or applications in Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In partially observable environments, reinforcement learning algorithms such as policy gradient and Q-learning may have multiple equilibria...

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development. It focuses on the theoretical aspects of reinforcement learning without linking to climate or ecological themes.
primary_category.quote: We show theoretically that the core problem is that in partially observed environments, an agent’s past actions induce a distribution on hidden states.

new_primary_category.quote: Prior work blames insufficient exploration, but suboptimal equilibria can arise despite full exploration and other favorable circumstances...
